blocks.content: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is the premier investigating agency of the Central Government.

items: CBI is NOT a statutory body; it was created via an executive resolution and derives its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.
CBI requires the consent of the respective State Government (general or specific consent) to exercise powers and jurisdiction inside a state.
The appointment mechanism for the CBI Director was modified under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, establishing a high-powered 3-member selection committee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Established in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962–1964).
The CBI is a non-statutory body and derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
It operates under the administrative control of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

The CBI Director is appointed based on recommendations of a 3-member committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge.
It serves as the National Central Bureau of Interpol in India, coordinating international law enforcement operations.
